## Summary

Eisman reviews a technology-led second-quarter rally already showing signs of reversal. He favors scarce semiconductor and power capacity over capital-hungry model builders, questions weak consulting and consumer turnarounds, and discusses financial-sector leadership. He criticizes Greenspan's regulatory legacy and argues that greater US economic dynamism favors US investments over Europe.

Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.

## Framework and tools

- Look inside sector returns to distinguish scarce suppliers from the buyers funding their growth.
- Capital intensity requires durable competitive protection to generate acceptable returns.
- Separate social-policy preferences from investment-return judgments.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- S&P 500, Nasdaq and eleven sector returns through June 24
- Individual stock quarter-to-date returns
- Micron earnings, forward P/E and supply outlook
- Capital raising and business-model comparison for hyperscalers

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman hosts the episode; guest turns are inferred from introductions and conversational context.
- Quarter review is explicitly an incomplete-quarter snapshot, not final June 30 performance.
- Micron EPS is rendered $251; primary disclosure is $25.11, so the caption numeral is unreliable.
- Captions render moat as moes and MOU as anou.
- Greenspan is repeatedly said to have retired in 2005; Federal Reserve history says January 31, 2006.
